faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.subtitle: Straight answers about the trial, AI articles, sources and publishing with Topiqu.

items.q: How does the free trial work?
items.a: Every new blog starts with a 14-day trial and 5 AI articles. Continue on Free and you try the Premium features with no card. Choose Pro or Premium during sign-up and Stripe asks for a card, but the first charge comes only after the 14 days — you can cancel before then.

items.q: What counts as an AI article?
items.a: Each article that AI writes for you uses one article from your allowance: 20 a month on Pro and 30 on Premium. Translations, fact-checks, prompt improvements, sentiment analysis and Search Console suggestions do not use articles. Purchased articles never expire; pack prices are listed above.

items.q: Where does the AI get its facts?
items.a: Topiqu combines live web research with your own knowledge base — notes, PDF and Word files, web pages or a whole sitemap. Private sources shape the text but are never cited publicly; only sources you mark as public can become citations. Before publishing, a review step checks claims against the sources, and the fact-check panel lets you re-check any article.
Only when you turn on automatic publishing. Otherwise every AI draft waits for you to review and edit it, and you can show an AI-content disclosure on the article.

items.q: How do I know whether answers cite me?
items.a: On Premium, Topiqu builds questions from your Search Console queries, articles and reader comments. It regularly checks whether OpenAI answers cite you and where competitors appear. Questions without your citation become article ideas. This is a sample of selected questions, not a record of private conversations.

items.q: Can I publish Topiqu articles on my existing website?
items.a: Yes. Use the hosted Topiqu publication, connect your domain, sync articles into WordPress with the Topiqu Sync plugin, or fetch them through the External API.
